viability_note: SPINE INTACT, case ships. Both halves verified fresh today. (1) Carbon Health's own blog is live and every core number is on the page verbatim, under 4 minutes vs 16, 88 percent, 2.5x, ten days, 600+ clinicians, full stack, consent language, patient summaries. (2) The JAMA Network Open study verified in full text, all thirteen requested data points confirmed. CRITICAL UNITS ANSWER, as demanded: the 0.90 hours after-hours documentation difference is PER WEEK. The article's own outcome-measure wording is 'The average amount of time I spend per week writing notes outside of clinic hours.' This is confirmed by internal arithmetic, 0.90 hours equals 54 minutes per week, which the authors themselves restate as 'the equivalent of 10.8 minutes saved per workday' over a 5 day week. c22 and c23 are therefore the SAME finding expressed two ways and must never be stacked. MAGNITUDE SANITY CHECK, the deck's whole thesis: Carbon Health's 16 minutes is PER VISIT chart-writing time, vendor self-measured. The study's 0.90 hours is PER WEEK of self-reported AFTER-HOURS note writing. Different units, different time bases, different populations, different systems, and different measurement methods (vendor internal instrumentation vs clinician survey recall). Any slide placing 12 saved minutes per visit beside 54 saved minutes per week without naming both bases must be killed. The honest framing the deck should carry is that the vendor measured the task and the independent study measured the week, and the week barely moved. THREE FINDINGS THAT CHANGE THE BRIEF. First, the bank's skepticism note is WRONG as written. It says the 30 percent more visits claim is 'NOT in the primary source'. It IS in Carbon Health's own Business Wire press release verbatim, one San Francisco pilot clinic, though it is absent from the engineering blog. This is a stronger honesty beat than the brief anticipated, the company made a volume claim on the wire and did not repeat it on its own technical blog. Use it as the discounted claim, never as an outcome. See c12. Second, the independent study measured ABRIDGE, a commercial vendor product, not Carbon Health's in-house build. The study is category evidence, not evidence about this company, and the deck must say so or it commits the aggregate-vs-specific error. See c24. Third, the JAMA URL supplied in the brief (fullarticle/2839148) is WRONG and resolves to an unrelated JAMA Cardiology myotonic dystrophy paper. The DOI redirects to fullarticle/2839542. Fix every outbound link. LOSSES, none fatal per the brief's own rule. All three Alaska local-proof sources and both failure-base-rate and trade-corroboration fetches failed today, so the translation slide has NO verified Alaska number and must be written as qualitative segment language only, or the showrunner must source new Alaska proof. Becker's returned 403 so no independent trade corroboration exists in this claim set, meaning every Carbon Health fact in the deck is vendor-sourced and must carry that label in the same breath per i-005. The deck's independent evidence is the JAMA study alone, which is sufficient because the thesis is precisely that the vendor and the independent literature disagree. NOT FACTS, ANALYSIS ONLY, no claim-ids, may not wear citations: that the two numbers measure different things and the operator should plan against the independent one; that acceptance rate is not accuracy; that ambient scribes buy back attention rather than throughput; any Anchorage clinic sizing or bottleneck mapping.
